productDefinition: Suites Blackbox turns Playwright system and E2E tests into behavioral verification gates by observing the running system's boundary effects and checking them against reviewed expectations.

specificationModel.ears: Normative requirements bind to executable flow IDs and receive runtime-backed requirement verdicts.
specificationModel.gherkin: Behavioral examples connect with executable Playwright or Blackbox DSL tests through generation, analysis, drift checks, and an experimental scaffold path.
specificationModel.relationship: EARS and Gherkin are complementary specification surfaces. Neither is required to use effect verification.

claims.claim: Blackbox adds runtime behavioral verification to Playwright system and E2E tests.
A response assertion and an effect assertion answer different questions: what came back and what the running system did at its boundaries.
The compose testbed can inject the Node OpenTelemetry bootstrap into compatible SUT containers during the test run without adding OpenTelemetry imports to application source.
A missing catalog entry can be baselined from observed effects; after review, the catalog entry becomes the persisted requires-and-forbids contract used by later runs.
toObserveEffects() checks inline effect expectations and toMatchCatalog() checks the flow's reviewed catalog entry using the same evaluation kernel.
Effect coverage reports whether reviewed required effects were observed and whether forbidden effects remained absent for exercised flows.
OMC/DC compares exercised decision arms with observed effect signatures and reports propagating, masking-candidate, coverage-gap, or undecidable verdicts.
Blackbox validates EARS requirements, binds requirement IDs to effect flow IDs, detects binding drift, and joins runtime effect coverage into requirement verdicts.
Requirement coverage emits proven, violated, unproven, and unbound verdicts and writes requirements/coverage.json.
JSON-capable CLI commands use a schema-versioned envelope with deterministic key ordering and distinct ok, findings, and error states.
Blackbox can analyze Playwright or Blackbox DSL tests, emit canonical Gherkin feature files, lint scenario structure, and detect source-to-feature drift.
Blackbox can scaffold a Blackbox DSL test with TODO bodies from a Gherkin feature file.
Blackbox supports concurrent Playwright workers by isolating worker-owned SUT state and merging worker evidence into canonical suite artifacts.
Effects, EARS requirement bindings, and Gherkin feature workflows can be adopted separately; the combined loop provides the strongest trace from intent to runtime verdict.
The current public path targets Node 22+, TypeScript, Playwright, Docker or a compatible container runtime, and Node SUT containers that the testbed can instrument.
